title: Ultrasound neuromodulation reveals distinct roles of the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex and anterior insula in learning
experiments_summary: The study employed a single-blinded, within-subject, counterbalanced 3-session offline transcranial ultrasonic stimulation (TUS) design with 29 healthy participants. Session 1 involved structural MRI (T1-weighted MPRAGE) acquisition for neuronavigation and pseudo-CT generation for personalized acoustic planning, plus task practice. The three subsequent sessions each involved an 80-second, 5 Hz-patterned TUS intervention (500 kHz fundamental frequency, 20 ms pulse duration, 10% duty cycle, ISPPA ~50 W/cm² in water, 400 pulses total) targeting either bilateral dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (dACC), bilateral anterior insula (aIns), or sham, followed within 10 minutes by a motivational Go/NoGo learning task. Target localization used individual T1-weighted MRI anatomical landmarks and acoustic/thermal simulations derived from pseudo-CT skull models. A bespoke CTX-500 NeuroFUS TPO system with a four-element annular transducer was used. Sham stimulation placed the transducer over the temporal region without ultrasound delivery, substituting bone-conduction headphone playback of an acoustically matched sound. Safety was monitored via acoustic simulation of mechanical index and CEM43 values, plus post-session and 24-48 hour adverse event questionnaires. The Go/NoGo task comprised 320 trials per session across four blocks, with participants learning via probabilistic feedback (80/20%) to associate Go or NoGo actions with Win or Avoid cues, using distinct cue sets per session to prevent carry-over. Behavioral analyses used mixed-effects logistic regression on Go/NoGo responses and repeat/switch choices as functions of required action, cue valence, TUS condition, and block half. A series of seven increasingly complex computational reinforcement learning (Q-learning) models were fit to the sham session data to isolate three Pavlovian bias parameters: a response bias (π), a learning bias (κ), and a persistence bias (φDIFF). Models were compared using Bayesian model selection with protected exceedance probabilities via the CBM toolbox. The best-fitting model (M7) was then fit to all three TUS conditions, and bias parameters were compared across conditions using one-way repeated-measures ANOVAs with paired t-tests and Bonferroni correction. Posterior predictive checks, parameter recovery, and model recovery analyses were conducted to validate model identifiability. Dose-response analyses correlated simulated acoustic pressure at target with parameter changes. Control analyses tested for effects of age, gender, session order, and session identity.
